2027-05-14.title: Saint Matthias, Apostle
readings: The lot fell on Matthias; and he was added to the eleven apostles
He raises the poor from the dust, to make them sit with the princes of his people (or: Alleluia)
You did not choose me but I chose you
2027-05-14.alt: Feast. The Gloria is said. The readings of Friday of the Seventh Week of Easter (Acts 25:13b–21; John 21:15–19) give way to those of the feast. St Matthias was kept on 24 February until the reform of the calendar in 1969, which moved him to 14 May, close to the days between the Ascension and Pentecost when he was chosen. Liturgical colour: red.
2027-05-14.verse: You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last,
theo: Of all the apostles, Matthias is the one we know least, and yet his feast falls at exactly the right moment. The Lord has ascended; the disciples have gone back to Jerusalem and are praying in the upper room “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus.” In those days of waiting, Peter stands up among about a hundred and twenty believers. There is a wound in the Twelve. Judas, who “was numbered among us and was allotted his share in this ministry,” has gone “to his own place.” Peter reads the tragedy in the light of the Psalms: “Let his homestead become desolate,” and “Let another take his position of overseer.” The number twelve is not a detail. Jesus chose twelve to stand for the twelve tribes of Israel, the whole People of God gathered anew, and he promised that they would sit on thrones judging those tribes (Luke 22:30). Before the Spirit comes and the Church goes out to the nations, the circle must be complete.

What kind of man must fill the empty place? Peter names the condition: “one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day when he was taken up from us.” Above all, “one of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection.” An apostle is not chosen for his talents or his eloquence, but because he was with Jesus and has seen him risen. Two names are put forward: “Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.” Then the whole community prays: “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen.” They cast lots, an ancient way in Israel of leaving the decision to God (“The lot is cast into the lap, but the decision is the Lord's alone,” Proverbs 16:33), and “the lot fell on Matthias; and he was added to the eleven apostles.” It is the last time lots are used in the New Testament. After Pentecost the Church will discern by the Holy Spirit, by prayer and by the laying on of hands.

The Psalm sings what happened to Matthias: “He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes, with the princes of his people.” An unknown disciple, who had followed Jesus quietly from the Jordan to the Mount of Olives without ever being named, is suddenly placed among the foundations of the Church. The book of Revelation will say that the wall of the holy city “has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.” Matthias's name is written there. Joseph Barsabbas was not chosen, and we hear no complaint from him; he too is part of the story, a reminder that God's choice is never a rejection of the one who serves elsewhere.

The Gospel tells us where every apostolic call begins: “You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.” Matthias did not campaign for the place; the Lord, who knows every heart, chose him. And the choice is an act of friendship: “I do not call you servants any longer … but I have called you friends.” The heart of the apostle's work is the commandment of love: “love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.” Of Matthias's later life we know almost nothing for certain. Eusebius records a tradition that he was one of the Seventy whom Jesus sent out (Luke 10:1). Ancient accounts send him to preach in Judea, in Cappadocia, or on the shores of the Black Sea, and say he died a martyr; the Abbey of St Matthias at Trier in Germany has honoured relics believed to be his since the Middle Ages. What is certain is enough: he was with Jesus, he saw him risen, he was chosen by the Lord, and he received the Holy Spirit with the others at Pentecost. His name means “gift of the Lord.”
conn: In Jewish custom a community of a hundred and twenty men could have its own council. Luke may be hinting that the little group in the upper room is already the new Israel, ready to act.

Acts 1:18–19 and Matthew 27:3–10 tell of Judas's death and of the field called Hakeldama, Field of Blood, in two different ways. The Lectionary omits these verses; Peter's point is not the gruesome detail but the empty place in the Twelve.
Psalm 69:25 (“Let his homestead become desolate”) and Psalm 109:8 (“Let another take his position of overseer”). The Greek word for that position, episkopē, later gives us the word bishop.

Jesus chose twelve “to be with him, and to be sent out” (Mark 3:14). They stand for the twelve tribes of Israel. When James the brother of John was killed (Acts 12:2), no one was chosen to replace him: the circle of witnesses had been completed, and the Church was now founded.
Israel used lots to divide the land (Joshua 18:6), to choose the priests' duties (1 Chronicles 24:5; Luke 1:9) and to discern God's will. The stones were shaken in a vessel until one fell out.
“Son of the Sabbath,” perhaps because he was born on a Sabbath; Justus was his Latin name. A Judas called Barsabbas, perhaps his brother, appears later as a leader in Jerusalem (Acts 15:22).
A short form of Mattathias, Hebrew Mattithiah, “gift of the Lord.” He is never mentioned again in the New Testament after Acts 1:26.

In the ancient world the “friends of the king” were his trusted counsellors, who knew his plans. Abraham was called the friend of God (Isaiah 41:8; James 2:23). Jesus gives that title to all his disciples.
The older Roman calendar kept St Matthias on 24 February (25 in a leap year). The Eastern Churches honour him on 9 August. The reform of 1969 moved the Roman feast to 14 May.
altar: The apostles chose Matthias while they were waiting for the Spirit in prayer, and he was immediately counted among those who “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” The Eucharist we celebrate today rests on that apostolic foundation; in the Eucharistic Prayer the Church names the apostles, and in the Roman Canon Matthias is named among the martyrs after the consecration.

“No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.” At the altar Jesus does not only tell us this; he gives his own Body and Blood for his friends, and makes us capable of loving as he loved.
outline: Show a team photograph with one empty place. Ask: what does it take to fill that place?
Point 1 · One must become a witness
The Twelve made whole before Pentecost.
Point 2 · Lord, you know everyone's heart
Prayer and the lot: leaving the choice to God.
Point 3 · You did not choose me
The call as a gift of friendship.
Point 4 · From the dust to the princes
An unknown disciple among the foundations.
Twelve names carved on the foundation stones of the holy city, one of them Matthias.
“You did not choose me but I chose you.”
live: Tell one person this week, simply and in your own words, why you believe that Jesus is risen.
Before an important decision this week, pray as the apostles did: Lord, you know everyone's heart; show me what you have chosen.
Like Matthias, who followed Jesus for years without being named, do one service in your parish that no one will notice.
Pray today for those whom the Lord is choosing as priests and religious, especially in your own parish and family.
fathers: See how Peter does everything with the common consent: nothing by his own authority alone, nothing by command. He was the first of the apostles, yet he made the whole community share in the choice. And they prayed first, because they wanted God to make the choice, not themselves.
You did not choose me: here is grace beyond words. What were we before Christ chose us, if not wicked? He did not choose us because we were good; he chose us so that we might become good.
Matthias taught, so it was handed down, that we must fight against the flesh and not give in to it, and must make the soul grow through faith and knowledge.
A lot is not something evil: in a matter where human beings are uncertain, it points to the will of God.
magis: The Lord gave his community a structure: the Twelve with Peter as their head, representing the twelve tribes of Israel.
The Church is apostolic: built on the foundation of the apostles, guarding their teaching, and guided by their successors.
The apostles took care to appoint successors; the bishops have by divine institution taken the place of the apostles as shepherds of the Church.
Vatican II: Christ established the apostles as a college; the mission entrusted to them will last until the end of the world.
Jesus makes charity the new commandment: “As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you; abide in my love.”
saints: A disciple who followed Jesus from his baptism to the Ascension, chosen by lot to take the place of Judas among the Twelve (Acts 1:26). Traditions place his preaching in Judea and further afield and say he died a martyr; relics believed to be his are venerated at Trier and in Rome. Patron of Trier.

15 May: Saturday of the Seventh Week of Easter, the last weekday of Easter; the Vigil of Pentecost in the evening. 16 May: PENTECOST SUNDAY. 17 May: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church (memorial); Ordinary Time resumes. 18 May: St John I (optional). 20 May: St Bernardine of Siena (optional). 21 May: St Christopher Magallanes and companions (optional). 22 May: St Rita of Cascia (optional).
2027-05-14.prayer: O God, who assigned Saint Matthias a place in the college of Apostles, grant us, through his intercession, that, rejoicing at your love for us, we may merit to be numbered among the elect. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you did not wait for us to choose you; you chose us and called us your friends. As you chose Matthias to be a witness of your resurrection, make us witnesses in our homes and workplaces. Teach us to pray before we decide, to serve without seeking a name, and to love one another as you have loved us. With Mary and the apostles we wait for your Spirit: come, Holy Spirit, and fill the empty places in our hearts and in your Church. Amen.

quick: After the Ascension the apostles, praying with Mary, chose Matthias by lot to take the place of Judas among the Twelve.
The one chosen had to have been with Jesus from his baptism to the Ascension and be a witness of the resurrection.
Jesus says: you did not choose me but I chose you; I call you friends; love one another as I have loved you.
2027-05-14.action: Tell one person today, in a sentence, why you believe that Jesus is risen.
2027-05-14.question: Do I see my faith as my own choice, or as the Lord's choice of me in friendship?
catechism: The Twelve, representing the tribes of Israel.
The apostolic Church built on the apostles.
Love one another as I have loved you.
kidsaint: Matthias followed Jesus for a long time, from the River Jordan to the day Jesus went up to heaven, but nobody wrote his name down. After Judas left, the apostles needed a twelfth apostle. They prayed, and God chose Matthias! Lesson: even if nobody notices you, Jesus sees you, and he has a special job just for you.
2027-05-14.special: St Matthias, Apostle. Feast: Gloria; red vestments; the weekday readings give way.
term: From the Greek apostolos, one who is sent. In the strict sense, the Twelve chosen by Jesus (with Matthias in the place of Judas), and Paul. The Church is called apostolic because she is built on their witness, keeps their teaching, and is led by their successors, the bishops.

family.explain: After Jesus went back to heaven, there were only eleven apostles, because Judas had left. Jesus had chosen twelve, so they needed one more. They chose two good men who had been with Jesus all the time, prayed to God, and asked him to show which one he wanted. God chose Matthias. Jesus says to us too: you did not choose me, I chose you, and I call you my friends.
family.intention: We pray for our bishop, who takes the place of the apostles today, and for young people whom Jesus is calling to be priests and sisters.
family.ask: Ask: “Jesus calls us his friends. What do good friends do for each other?”

illus: In cricket there is a player called the twelfth man. He comes to every match, carries the drinks, and waits on the edge of the field, often without being noticed. When a player is injured, he is the one who runs in to take the empty place. Matthias was a little like that: for years he followed Jesus at the edge of the story, never named. When the place among the Twelve was empty, he was ready, because he had been there all along. But unlike a twelfth man, he did not step in for a while; the Lord chose him for life.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you chose Matthias to be a witness of your resurrection. You have chosen us too and called us friends. Fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: One of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection (Acts 1:22). How am I a witness to the risen Jesus in my daily life?
Lord, you know everyone's heart (Acts 1:24). Do I pray before I make important decisions?
You did not choose me but I chose you (John 15:16). How does it change me to know that the Lord chose me?
pm.resp: He raises the poor from the dust, to make them sit with princes.
interc: For our Pope and all the bishops, successors of the apostles, that they may be faithful witnesses of the resurrection.
For those who serve the Church without being noticed, that the Lord may reward their faithfulness.
For young people discerning a vocation, that they may hear the Lord's choice and answer generously.
For all who must make difficult decisions, that they may seek God's will in prayer.
For our group, that we may love one another as Jesus loved us, and wait together for the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you completed the college of the apostles by choosing Saint Matthias. Keep your Church faithful to their witness, and number us among your friends. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate an apostle who is mentioned by name only twice in the whole Bible, both times in one chapter of the Acts of the Apostles. We know almost nothing of his words or his travels. And yet Matthias is one of the twelve foundations of the Church.

The apostles had returned from the Mount of Olives and were praying in the upper room with Mary and the other women. There was an empty place. Judas, who had been one of them, had gone to his own place. Jesus had chosen twelve, for the twelve tribes of Israel. Before the Holy Spirit came, the circle had to be complete.

Peter says what kind of person is needed: one who had been with Jesus from the baptism of John to the Ascension, and who could become a witness with us to his resurrection (Acts 1:22). Not the cleverest, not the richest, not the most popular. The one who had stayed with Jesus, and had seen him alive.

Then the community did something we often forget to do: they prayed before they decided. Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen (Acts 1:24). They did not want their own choice; they wanted the Lord's. And the lot fell on Matthias. How many of our family quarrels and wrong decisions would be avoided if we prayed like this first?

In the Gospel Jesus tells us that this is how every vocation works. You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last (John 15:16). Our faith is first of all the Lord's choice of us. And he chooses us as friends: I do not call you servants any longer, but I have called you friends. The mark of his friends is love: love one another as I have loved you.

Perhaps you feel like Matthias before that day: following Jesus quietly, never noticed, never named. Do not be discouraged. The Lord sees you. He raises the poor from the dust to make them sit with princes. Stay with him, be a witness of his resurrection where you are, and when he calls, be ready. St Matthias, pray for us, and with Mary and the apostles, let us pray: Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Matthias followed Jesus for a long, long time, but nobody wrote his name in the Gospels. He was a quiet friend of Jesus. When the apostles needed one more, they prayed, and God chose Matthias!
Jesus says to you: I chose you, and you are my friend. Even when nobody notices you, Jesus sees you. Say: Thank you, Jesus, for choosing me!

intro: Theme: “You did not choose me but I chose you.”
St Matthias, the quiet disciple chosen to complete the Twelve as a witness of the resurrection.

sub: An empty place among the Twelve.
Twelve for the tribes of Israel.
Seen with Jesus, seen him risen.
q: You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
So one of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us … one of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection.
points.apply: This week, tell one person in simple words what the risen Jesus means to you.

q: For the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Then they prayed and said, “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen
points.apply: Before every important decision this week, stop and pray: Lord, you know the heart; show me what you have chosen.

q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last,
points.apply: Each morning this week, thank Jesus for choosing you, and ask what fruit he wants from you that day.

points.h: From the dust to the princes
q: He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes, with the princes of his people.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
points.apply: Thank someone in your parish whose service usually goes unnoticed.

concl: Matthias was chosen not for fame or gifts but because he had stayed with Jesus and seen him risen.
The Lord who chose him chooses us as friends, and sends us to bear fruit that will last.
2027-05-14.resolve: Pray before your next important decision, and tell someone this week why you believe that Jesus is risen.
